meta.designPrinciple: Tactile, but never at the cost of legibility. The soft-shadow language is reserved for exactly one control the user actually presses -- everything that carries meaning (text, icons, message content) uses full-contrast tokens regardless of how the rest of the surface looks.
meta.removedElement: First draft gave every message bubble the embossed dual-shadow treatment, matching the send button. Per the family's own accessibility flag (style-taxonomy.md), that's structurally in tension with legible text at that density -- a whole thread of soft-shadowed bubbles reads as a texture, not as distinguishable messages. Cut it down to exactly one embossed control (the send button); message bubbles are flat with a hairline border instead.

meta_a11y_flag: ACCESSIBILITY RISK, surfaced per style-taxonomy.md: neumorphism's signature soft embossing relies on low-contrast surface-on-surface color relationships, structurally in tension with WCAG AA text contrast and with distinguishing interactive from static elements. This theme mitigates by restricting the embossed treatment to a single focal control (send button) and giving every text/icon token full contrast against the flat canvas -- not by pretending the tension doesn't exist.

reducedMotion.strategy: disable the send button's press-depth transition, keep instant state swap

iconography.styleDescriptor: 1.75px stroke, no fill, full-contrast regardless of surrounding emboss

elevationScale.shadow: none -- flat with 1px border, not embossed (see meta.removedElement)
